            psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -qtAX -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -v "database=$database" -d "$1"
          }
          timescaledb="$(sql "$database" <<'SQL'
          SELECT 1 FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'timescaledb';
          SQL
          )"
          extensions="$(sql "$database" <<'SQL'
          SELECT format('CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS %I CASCADE;', extname)
            FROM pg_extension WHERE extname NOT IN ('plpgsql', 'timescaledb') ORDER BY oid;
          SQL
          )"
          sql "$maintenance" >/dev/null <<'SQL'
          SELECT format('CREATE DATABASE %I OWNER %I TEMPLATE template0 ENCODING %L LC_COLLATE %L LC_CTYPE %L',
                   datname, pg_get_userbyid(datdba), pg_encoding_to_char(encoding), datcollate, datctype)
                 || CASE fields ->> 'datlocprovider'
                      WHEN 'i' THEN format(' LOCALE_PROVIDER icu ICU_LOCALE %L', coalesce(fields ->> 'datlocale', fields ->> 'daticulocale'))
                        || CASE WHEN fields ->> 'daticurules' IS NULL THEN '' ELSE format(' ICU_RULES %L', fields ->> 'daticurules') END
                      WHEN 'b' THEN format(' LOCALE_PROVIDER builtin BUILTIN_LOCALE %L', fields ->> 'datlocale')
                      WHEN 'c' THEN ' LOCALE_PROVIDER libc'
                      ELSE ''
                    END AS create_database
            FROM pg_database d, to_jsonb(d) AS fields WHERE datname = :'database' \gset
          DROP DATABASE :"database" WITH (FORCE);
          SELECT :'create_database' \gexec
          SQL
          if [ -n "$timescaledb" ]; then
            echo "CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb CASCADE;" | sql "$database" >/dev/null
          fi
          if [ -n "$extensions" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$extensions" | sql "$database" >/dev/null
          fi
        - dokku-postgres-reset
        - "{{ .Database }}"
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
        PGOPTIONS: "-c client_min_messages=warning"

  # the templates every new database is copied from. postgres is left out: it
  # is only the default database, and a service named after it works
  reserved_names: [template0, template1]

---
# postgres with the pgvector extension, on the image pgvector publishes. It is
# a definition of its own rather than an image handed to the plain postgres
# ones because its tags write the major as pg17 rather than leading with it, so
# the version alone never placed it on the right data directory
services:
  postgres:
    image: "{{ .Image }}:{{ .ImageVersion }}"

    # the image creates the database and the account from these during its own
    # initialisation, which is why there is no step afterwards to make them
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: "{{ .Database }}"
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

    # ssl is turned on by the server's own options rather than by editing the
    # configuration file it writes during initialisation. The bash plugin has
    # to pause the service, patch that file and start it again, because the
    # file does not exist until the service has run once.
    command:
      - postgres
      - -c
      - ssl=on
      - -c
      - "ssl_cert_file={{ .Target.certs }}/server.crt"
      - -c
      - "ssl_key_file={{ .Target.certs }}/server.key"
      - -c
      - ssl_ciphers=AES256+EECDH:AES256+EDH

    volumes:
      # postgres moved its data directory up one level in eighteen
      - type: bind
        source: "{{ .HostRoot }}/data"
        target: /var/lib/postgresql
      - type: bind
        source: "{{ .HostRoot }}/certs"
        target: /certs

    ports:
      - name: native
        target: 5432
        primary: true

x-dokku:
  plugin: postgres
  title: Postgres
  scheme: postgres

  # DATABASE rather than POSTGRES: a linked app gets DATABASE_URL, which is
  # what postgres, mysql and mariadb all hand over
  alias: DATABASE
  alt_alias: DOKKU_POSTGRES

  # the account is the image's own superuser rather than one named for the
  # service, which is what the bash plugin hands over
  dsn: "{{ .Scheme }}://postgres:{{ .Secret.password }}@{{ .Host }}:{{ .Port.native }}/{{ .Database }}"

  wait: native

  secrets:
    password:
      file: PASSWORD
      length: 16
      env: SERVICE_PASSWORD

      # the image only reads POSTGRES_PASSWORD when it makes the cluster, so a
      # new password is given to the role by the server itself. The statement
      # is written to psql's stdin rather than passed as an argument, so the
      # password stays out of the container's process table. Every postgres
      # definition carries the same text, which a test holds them to.
      change:
        exec:
          - sh
          - -c
          - |
            set -e
            password="$(printf '%s' "$NEW_PASSWORD" | sed "s/'/''/g")"
            printf "ALTER ROLE postgres PASSWORD '%s';\n" "$password" |
              psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -qtAX -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d postgres >/dev/null
          - dokku-postgres-change-password
        env:
          PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
          NEW_PASSWORD: "{{ .NewSecret }}"

  hooks:
    pre_create:
      # the certificate, made before the service runs rather than after. It is
      # left alone once it exists, so a service keeps the identity it was
      # created with rather than being given a new one each time its container
      # is remade.
      user: "0"
      entrypoint: ""
      volumes:
        - type: bind
          source: "{{ .HostRoot }}/certs"
          target: /certs
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        # postgres refuses to start on a key anyone but its own user can read
        # the two files change hands, but the directory holding them stays
        # with dokku: postgres only ever stats the key, and a directory owned
        # by the server would leave destroy unable to unlink what is inside it
        - >-
          test -f /certs/server.key ||
          (openssl req -new -newkey rsa:4096 -x509 -days 365000 -nodes
          -out /certs/server.crt -keyout /certs/server.key -batch >/dev/null 2>&1);
          chown 999:999 /certs/server.key /certs/server.crt &&
          chmod 600 /certs/server.key && chmod 644 /certs/server.crt

  # a service moved onto this definition from another postgres definition has
  # its data carried across: a major version cannot read another's cluster, and
  # a flavor's extensions are only in its own image. The old data directory is
  # kept aside under the service root until upgrade-cleanup removes it.
  upgrade:
    migrate: true

    # every database and role the cluster holds, rather than the one database
    # the export subcommand dumps, so that nothing an app or an operator made
    # beside it is left behind in the data kept aside. --clean drops what the
    # new cluster made of its own before it is made again from the dump.
    export:
      exec: ["pg_dumpall", "-h", "localhost", "-U", "postgres", "-w", "--clean", "--if-exists"]
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

    # the dump is replayed from the maintenance database, which pg_dumpall
    # drops and makes again from whichever database it last connected to. The
    # superuser it is replayed as already exists and cannot be dropped, so the
    # two statements that would try are left out of the roles at the top of the
    # dump, before its first \connect and so before any of its rows.
    #
    # an image may make template databases of its own when the cluster is
    # first made, as postgis does with template_postgis, and a template cannot
    # be dropped. pg_dumpall only clears template1's flag before dropping it, so
    # every other template the new cluster has is made an ordinary database
    # first. The dump makes each template the old cluster had a template again,
    # and one only the new image made stays an ordinary database.
    #
    # timescaledb's catalog has to be restored with its workers stopped and
    # its triggers off, which timescaledb_pre_restore does for a database. The
    # dump drops and makes every database again, so restoring is also turned on
    # for the whole server until the dump is in, and each database is told the
    # restore is over afterwards. Every postgres definition carries the same
    # text, which a test holds them to, and the timescaledb steps do nothing on
    # an image without the extension.
    import:
      stdin: true
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          set -e
          sql() {
            psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -qtAX -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d "$1"
          }
          databases() {
            echo "SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datallowconn ORDER BY datname;" | sql postgres
          }
          timescaledb="$(echo "SELECT 1 FROM pg_available_extensions WHERE name = 'timescaledb';" | sql postgres)"
          if [ -n "$timescaledb" ]; then
            echo "ALTER SYSTEM SET timescaledb.restoring = on;" | sql postgres >/dev/null
            echo "SELECT pg_reload_conf();" | sql postgres >/dev/null
            for database in $(databases); do
              echo "SELECT timescaledb_pre_restore() FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'timescaledb';" | sql "$database" >/dev/null
            done
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "SELECT format('ALTER DATABASE %I IS_TEMPLATE false', datname) FROM pg_database WHERE datistemplate AND datname NOT IN ('template0', 'template1') \gexec" | sql postgres >/dev/null
          status=0
          awk -v user=postgres '
            /^\\connect / { connected = 1 }
            !connected && ($0 == "CREATE ROLE " user ";" || $0 == "DROP ROLE IF EXISTS " user ";") { next }
            { print }
          ' | psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d postgres >/dev/null || status=$?
          if [ -n "$timescaledb" ]; then
            echo "ALTER SYSTEM RESET timescaledb.restoring;" | sql postgres >/dev/null
            echo "SELECT pg_reload_conf();" | sql postgres >/dev/null
            for database in $(databases); do
              echo "SELECT timescaledb_post_restore() FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'timescaledb';" | sql "$database" >/dev/null
              echo "ALTER DATABASE \"$database\" RESET timescaledb.restoring;" | sql "$database" >/dev/null
            done
          fi
          exit "$status"
        - dokku-postgres-upgrade-import
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
        PGOPTIONS: "-c client_min_messages=warning"

    # what the data needs of the image a service is moved onto, read and
    # checked before anything of the service is touched. timescaledb only
    # restores a dump into the version of the extension that made it, so each
    # version a database runs is printed, and the check compares it with the
    # version the new image installs. Every postgres definition carries the
    # same text, which a test holds them to, and both do nothing where the
    # extension is not installed.
    requires:
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          set -e
          sql() {
            psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -qtAX -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d "$1"
          }
          versions=""
          for database in $(echo "SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datallowconn ORDER BY datname;" | sql postgres); do
            versions="$versions$(echo "SELECT 'timescaledb ' || extversion FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'timescaledb';" | sql "$database")
          "
          done
          printf '%s' "$versions" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u
        - dokku-postgres-upgrade-requires
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
    check:
      stdin: true
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          set -e
          while read -r name version; do
            [ -n "$name" ] || continue
            sharedir="$(pg_config --sharedir 2>/dev/null || true)"
            control="$sharedir/extension/$name.control"
            if [ -z "$sharedir" ] || [ ! -f "$control" ]; then
              echo "the data uses $name $version, which the new image does not install" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            installs="$(sed -n "s/^default_version *= *'\(.*\)'.*/\1/p" "$control")"
            if [ "$installs" != "$version" ]; then
              echo "the data uses $name $version, but the new image installs $name $installs, and a dump is only restored into the version that made it. Run ALTER EXTENSION $name UPDATE in each database on the current definition, or upgrade onto an image that installs $name $version" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
        - dokku-postgres-upgrade-check

  # the certificate the server was started with, so that a client off the host
  # can verify it is talking to this service. Read from the running container
  # rather than the host, which keeps it following a moved certs volume
  custom_commands:
    certificate:
      description: print the certificate the {{.Title}} service encrypts connections with
      documentation: |
        print the certificate the {{.Title}} service encrypts connections with
        > NOTE: the service must be running
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:certificate lollipop
        save it to verify the server from a client off the host
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:certificate lollipop > server.crt
      exec: ["cat", "{{ .Target.certs }}/server.crt"]

    # the data an upgrade kept aside belongs to the postgres user, so it is
    # removed from a container running as root rather than from the host. Only
    # the directories an upgrade names are matched, and each is printed as it
    # goes
    upgrade-cleanup:
      description: remove the data an upgrade across a major version kept aside
      documentation: |
        remove the data an upgrade across a major version kept aside
        > NOTE: the service must be running
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:upgrade-cleanup lollipop
      mode: sidecar
      user: "0"
      entrypoint: ""
      volumes:
        - type: bind
          source: "{{ .HostRoot }}"
          target: /service
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        - find /service -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'data.*' -print -exec rm -rf {} +

  # written the way a command's documentation is: every sentence ends in a
  # period, since prose lines run together, and inline code is quoted
  documentation:
    - title: Encrypting connections with TLS
      body: |
        every {{.Title}} service is created with a self-signed certificate, and the server encrypts any connection whose client asks it to.
        the certificate and its key are kept in '/var/lib/dokku/services/{{.CommandPrefix}}/lollipop/certs', and are kept when the service is rebuilt or upgraded.
        clients such as psql ask for an encrypted connection by default, but fall back to an unencrypted one when the server does not offer it.
        to refuse an unencrypted connection instead, add 'sslmode=require' to the dsn the service is exposed at:
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:info lollipop --exposed-dsn
            postgres://postgres:PASSWORD@db.example.com:5432/lollipop?sslmode=require
        to also check that the client is talking to this service, save its certificate and have the client verify the server with it.
        the certificate names no host, so 'sslmode=verify-ca' works where 'sslmode=verify-full' does not:
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:certificate lollipop > server.crt
            postgres://postgres:PASSWORD@db.example.com:5432/lollipop?sslmode=verify-ca&sslrootcert=server.crt
        to use a certificate of your own, write it and its key over the ones the service was created with as root, and restart the service.
        writing over the files rather than replacing them keeps the owner and mode the server needs to read its key:
            sudo sh -c 'cat server.crt > /var/lib/dokku/services/{{.CommandPrefix}}/lollipop/certs/server.crt'
            sudo sh -c 'cat server.key > /var/lib/dokku/services/{{.CommandPrefix}}/lollipop/certs/server.key'
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:restart lollipop

    # the image makes the database from the environment its first start sees,
    # so the only way to choose these is the custom env the service is made with
    - title: Choosing the database encoding and locale
      body: |
        the database is made the first time the service starts, with the encoding and locale of its container, which are utf8 and 'en_US.utf8' unless the custom environment says otherwise.
        a custom environment that only sets 'LC_ALL=C' leaves the database in the SQL_ASCII encoding, which stores bytes rather than utf8 text.
        to choose both, give the arguments 'initdb' takes in POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS when the service is created:
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:create lollipop --custom-env "POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS=--encoding=UTF8 --locale=C"
        they are only read when the data directory is first made, so changing the custom environment of an existing service leaves its database as it was.
        to move a database to another encoding or locale, create a service with the new ones and import an export of the old service into it:
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:export lollipop > lollipop.dump
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:create lollipop-utf8 --custom-env "POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS=--encoding=UTF8 --locale=C"
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:import lollipop-utf8 < lollipop.dump

    # what an upgrade across a major version does with the data, which is not
    # something the upgrade command's own documentation can say for every
    # datastore
    - title: Upgrading across a major version
      body: |
        an upgrade that moves a service to another major version, or onto another flavor, carries its data across rather than mounting it where the new version would not read it.
        the linked apps are stopped while the data is copied, so the upgrade has to be given '--restart-apps':
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:upgrade lollipop --definition postgres-18 --restart-apps
        onto a newer major of the official image the data is copied with 'pg_upgrade', which needs as much free disk as the data takes up.
        every other move exports every database and role from the old version with 'pg_dumpall' and replays it into the new one.
        a move that fails puts the service back on the version it ran, with the data it had.
        the old data is kept in a 'data.<definition>.<timestamp>' directory beside the service's data, and is removed once the upgrade is confirmed:
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:upgrade-cleanup lollipop

  commands:
    # the password goes in PGPASSWORD rather than on the command line, which is
    # what the bash plugin does too
    connect:
      exec: ["psql", "-v", "ON_ERROR_STOP=1", "-h", "localhost", "-U", "postgres", "{{ .Database }}"]
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
        LANG: C.UTF-8
        LC_ALL: C.UTF-8

    export:
      extra_args: true
      exec: ["pg_dump", "-Fc", "--no-acl", "--no-owner", "-h", "localhost", "-U", "postgres", "-w", "{{ .Database }}"]
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

      # every database but the templates, and the maintenance database unless
      # it is the service's own, as plain sql that psql loads. pg_dumpall is
      # not used because it dumps the roles too, and loading them would set the
      # postgres password to the one the dump was taken with, leaving every
      # linked app holding the wrong one. Each database is dropped and made
      # again from template0 with the encoding and locale it had, the way reset
      # makes it, and marked as restoring until it is loaded, which keeps the
      # timescaledb background workers from writing into its catalog while the
      # dump copies it back. The databases are owned by postgres, as the dump
      # carries no owners. The locale columns are read through the row as json,
      # since each major names them differently and fourteen has none of them:
      # a column one major lacks reads as null rather than failing the query.
      # Every postgres definition carries the same text, which a test holds
      # them to.
      all_databases:
        extra_args: true
        exec:
          - sh
          - -c
          - |
            set -e
            own="$1"
            shift
            sql() {
              psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -qtAX -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d template1 "$@"
            }
            databases="$(sql -v "own=$own" <<'SQL'
            SELECT datname FROM pg_database
             WHERE NOT datistemplate AND (datname <> 'postgres' OR datname = :'own')
             ORDER BY datname;
            SQL
            )"
            printf '%s\n' "$databases" | while IFS= read -r database; do
              sql -v "database=$database" <<'SQL'
            SELECT format('DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS %I WITH (FORCE);', datname) || chr(10)
                || format('CREATE DATABASE %I TEMPLATE template0 ENCODING %L LC_COLLATE %L LC_CTYPE %L',
                          datname, pg_encoding_to_char(encoding), datcollate, datctype)
                || CASE fields ->> 'datlocprovider'
                     WHEN 'i' THEN format(' LOCALE_PROVIDER icu ICU_LOCALE %L', coalesce(fields ->> 'datlocale', fields ->> 'daticulocale'))
                       || CASE WHEN fields ->> 'daticurules' IS NULL THEN '' ELSE format(' ICU_RULES %L', fields ->> 'daticurules') END
                     WHEN 'b' THEN format(' LOCALE_PROVIDER builtin BUILTIN_LOCALE %L', fields ->> 'datlocale')
                     WHEN 'c' THEN ' LOCALE_PROVIDER libc'
                     ELSE ''
                   END || ';' || chr(10)
                || format('ALTER DATABASE %I SET timescaledb.restoring = %L;', datname, 'on') || chr(10)
                || format('\connect %I', datname)
              FROM pg_database d, to_jsonb(d) AS fields WHERE datname = :'database';
            SQL
              pg_dump -Fp --no-acl --no-owner -h localhost -U postgres -w "$@" "$database"
              sql -v "database=$database" <<'SQL'
            SELECT format('ALTER DATABASE %I RESET timescaledb.restoring;', datname) || chr(10)
                || 'SELECT pg_catalog.format(''SELECT %I.timescaledb_post_restore();'', n.nspname)'
                || ' FROM pg_catalog.pg_extension e JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.oid = e.extnamespace'
                || ' WHERE e.extname = ''timescaledb'' \gexec'
              FROM pg_database WHERE datname = :'database';
            SQL
            done
          - dokku-postgres-export-all
          - "{{ .Database }}"
        env:
          PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

    import:
      extra_args: true
      stdin: true
      exec: ["pg_restore", "-h", "localhost", "-cO", "--if-exists", "-d", "{{ .Database }}", "-U", "postgres", "-w"]
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

      # a dump of every database, which drops and makes each database in it
      # again, so it is loaded from template1 rather than from any database it
      # might drop. A load that stops part way leaves a database it made marked
      # as restoring, where timescaledb runs no background workers, so the mark
      # is cleared whether the load worked or not. Every postgres definition
      # carries the same text, which a test holds them to.
      all_databases:
        extra_args: true
        stdin: true
        exec:
          - sh
          - -c
          - |
            status=0
            psql -X -q -o /dev/null -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -h localhost -U postgres -w -d template1 "$@" || status=$?
            psql -X -q -o /dev/null -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -h localhost -U postgres -w -d template1 <<'SQL' || exit $?
            SELECT format('ALTER DATABASE %I RESET timescaledb.restoring', d.datname)
              FROM pg_db_role_setting s JOIN pg_database d ON d.oid = s.setdatabase
             WHERE s.setrole = 0 AND 'timescaledb.restoring=on' = ANY (s.setconfig) \gexec
            SQL
            exit "$status"
          - dokku-postgres-import-all
        env:
          PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

    # the database is dropped and made again from template0 with the owner,
    # encoding and locale it had, rather than emptied, so nothing an app made in
    # it survives. WITH (FORCE) ends the sessions linked apps hold open, which
    # would otherwise refuse the drop. The extensions it had are made again at
    # the image's default version, timescaledb first and in a session of its
    # own, since the rest may build on it and it expects to be the first thing a
    # session loads. Settings made with ALTER DATABASE and grants on the database
    # itself are not carried over.
    #
    # the create statement is read before anything is dropped, so a database
    # that cannot be described is left alone. The locale columns are read
    # through the row as json, the way the export of every database reads them,
    # since each major names them differently. A service named postgres has the
    # maintenance database as its own, so the drop is run from template1 instead.
    # Written inline rather than shipped as a script, since a script is only
    # mounted into a container made after it was added, and a reset runs in the
    # container the service already has. Every postgres definition carries the
    # same text, which a test holds them to.
    reset:
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          set -e
          database="$1"
          maintenance=postgres
          if [ "$database" = postgres ]; then
            maintenance=template1
          fi
          sql() {
            psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -qtAX -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -v "database=$database" -d "$1"
          }
          timescaledb="$(sql "$database" <<'SQL'
          SELECT 1 FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'timescaledb';
          SQL
          )"
          extensions="$(sql "$database" <<'SQL'
          SELECT format('CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS %I CASCADE;', extname)
            FROM pg_extension WHERE extname NOT IN ('plpgsql', 'timescaledb') ORDER BY oid;
          SQL
          )"
          sql "$maintenance" >/dev/null <<'SQL'
          SELECT format('CREATE DATABASE %I OWNER %I TEMPLATE template0 ENCODING %L LC_COLLATE %L LC_CTYPE %L',
                   datname, pg_get_userbyid(datdba), pg_encoding_to_char(encoding), datcollate, datctype)
                 || CASE fields ->> 'datlocprovider'
                      WHEN 'i' THEN format(' LOCALE_PROVIDER icu ICU_LOCALE %L', coalesce(fields ->> 'datlocale', fields ->> 'daticulocale'))
                        || CASE WHEN fields ->> 'daticurules' IS NULL THEN '' ELSE format(' ICU_RULES %L', fields ->> 'daticurules') END
                      WHEN 'b' THEN format(' LOCALE_PROVIDER builtin BUILTIN_LOCALE %L', fields ->> 'datlocale')
                      WHEN 'c' THEN ' LOCALE_PROVIDER libc'
                      ELSE ''
                    END AS create_database
            FROM pg_database d, to_jsonb(d) AS fields WHERE datname = :'database' \gset
          DROP DATABASE :"database" WITH (FORCE);
          SELECT :'create_database' \gexec
          SQL
          if [ -n "$timescaledb" ]; then
            echo "CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb CASCADE;" | sql "$database" >/dev/null
          fi
          if [ -n "$extensions" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$extensions" | sql "$database" >/dev/null
          fi
        - dokku-postgres-reset
        - "{{ .Database }}"
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
        PGOPTIONS: "-c client_min_messages=warning"

  # the templates every new database is copied from. postgres is left out: it
  # is only the default database, and a service named after it works
  reserved_names: [template0, template1]

---
# postgres with the postgis extension, on the image postgis publishes. It is a
# definition of its own so that the image is followed by dependabot and a bare
# upgrade has a newest postgis to move to
services:
  postgres:
    image: "{{ .Image }}:{{ .ImageVersion }}"

    # the image creates the database and the account from these during its own
    # initialisation, which is why there is no step afterwards to make them
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: "{{ .Database }}"
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

    # ssl is turned on by the server's own options rather than by editing the
    # configuration file it writes during initialisation. The bash plugin has
    # to pause the service, patch that file and start it again, because the
    # file does not exist until the service has run once.
    command:
      - postgres
      - -c
      - ssl=on
      - -c
      - "ssl_cert_file={{ .Target.certs }}/server.crt"
      - -c
      - "ssl_key_file={{ .Target.certs }}/server.key"
      - -c
      - ssl_ciphers=AES256+EECDH:AES256+EDH

    volumes:
      # where postgres kept its data before eighteen, which is the whole
      # reason this line has a definition of its own
      - type: bind
        source: "{{ .HostRoot }}/data"
        target: /var/lib/postgresql/data
      - type: bind
        source: "{{ .HostRoot }}/certs"
        target: /certs

    ports:
      - name: native
        target: 5432
        primary: true

x-dokku:
  plugin: postgres
  title: Postgres
  scheme: postgres

  # DATABASE rather than POSTGRES: a linked app gets DATABASE_URL, which is
  # what postgres, mysql and mariadb all hand over
  alias: DATABASE
  alt_alias: DOKKU_POSTGRES

  # the account is the image's own superuser rather than one named for the
  # service, which is what the bash plugin hands over
  dsn: "{{ .Scheme }}://postgres:{{ .Secret.password }}@{{ .Host }}:{{ .Port.native }}/{{ .Database }}"

  wait: native

  secrets:
    password:
      file: PASSWORD
      length: 16
      env: SERVICE_PASSWORD

      # the image only reads POSTGRES_PASSWORD when it makes the cluster, so a
      # new password is given to the role by the server itself. The statement
      # is written to psql's stdin rather than passed as an argument, so the
      # password stays out of the container's process table. Every postgres
      # definition carries the same text, which a test holds them to.
      change:
        exec:
          - sh
          - -c
          - |
            set -e
            password="$(printf '%s' "$NEW_PASSWORD" | sed "s/'/''/g")"
            printf "ALTER ROLE postgres PASSWORD '%s';\n" "$password" |
              psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -qtAX -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d postgres >/dev/null
          - dokku-postgres-change-password
        env:
          PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
          NEW_PASSWORD: "{{ .NewSecret }}"

  hooks:
    pre_create:
      # the certificate, made before the service runs rather than after. It is
      # left alone once it exists, so a service keeps the identity it was
      # created with rather than being given a new one each time its container
      # is remade.
      user: "0"
      entrypoint: ""
      volumes:
        - type: bind
          source: "{{ .HostRoot }}/certs"
          target: /certs
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        # postgres refuses to start on a key anyone but its own user can read
        # the two files change hands, but the directory holding them stays
        # with dokku: postgres only ever stats the key, and a directory owned
        # by the server would leave destroy unable to unlink what is inside it
        - >-
          test -f /certs/server.key ||
          (openssl req -new -newkey rsa:4096 -x509 -days 365000 -nodes
          -out /certs/server.crt -keyout /certs/server.key -batch >/dev/null 2>&1);
          chown 999:999 /certs/server.key /certs/server.crt &&
          chmod 600 /certs/server.key && chmod 644 /certs/server.crt

  # a service moved onto this definition from another postgres definition has
  # its data carried across: a major version cannot read another's cluster, and
  # a flavor's extensions are only in its own image. The old data directory is
  # kept aside under the service root until upgrade-cleanup removes it.
  upgrade:
    migrate: true

    # every database and role the cluster holds, rather than the one database
    # the export subcommand dumps, so that nothing an app or an operator made
    # beside it is left behind in the data kept aside. --clean drops what the
    # new cluster made of its own before it is made again from the dump.
    export:
      exec: ["pg_dumpall", "-h", "localhost", "-U", "postgres", "-w", "--clean", "--if-exists"]
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

    # the dump is replayed from the maintenance database, which pg_dumpall
    # drops and makes again from whichever database it last connected to. The
    # superuser it is replayed as already exists and cannot be dropped, so the
    # two statements that would try are left out of the roles at the top of the
    # dump, before its first \connect and so before any of its rows.
    #
    # an image may make template databases of its own when the cluster is
    # first made, as postgis does with template_postgis, and a template cannot
    # be dropped. pg_dumpall only clears template1's flag before dropping it, so
    # every other template the new cluster has is made an ordinary database
    # first. The dump makes each template the old cluster had a template again,
    # and one only the new image made stays an ordinary database.
    #
    # timescaledb's catalog has to be restored with its workers stopped and
    # its triggers off, which timescaledb_pre_restore does for a database. The
    # dump drops and makes every database again, so restoring is also turned on
    # for the whole server until the dump is in, and each database is told the
    # restore is over afterwards. Every postgres definition carries the same
    # text, which a test holds them to, and the timescaledb steps do nothing on
    # an image without the extension.
    import:
      stdin: true
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          set -e
          sql() {
            psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -qtAX -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d "$1"
          }
          databases() {
            echo "SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datallowconn ORDER BY datname;" | sql postgres
          }
          timescaledb="$(echo "SELECT 1 FROM pg_available_extensions WHERE name = 'timescaledb';" | sql postgres)"
          if [ -n "$timescaledb" ]; then
            echo "ALTER SYSTEM SET timescaledb.restoring = on;" | sql postgres >/dev/null
            echo "SELECT pg_reload_conf();" | sql postgres >/dev/null
            for database in $(databases); do
              echo "SELECT timescaledb_pre_restore() FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'timescaledb';" | sql "$database" >/dev/null
            done
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "SELECT format('ALTER DATABASE %I IS_TEMPLATE false', datname) FROM pg_database WHERE datistemplate AND datname NOT IN ('template0', 'template1') \gexec" | sql postgres >/dev/null
          status=0
          awk -v user=postgres '
            /^\\connect / { connected = 1 }
            !connected && ($0 == "CREATE ROLE " user ";" || $0 == "DROP ROLE IF EXISTS " user ";") { next }
            { print }
          ' | psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d postgres >/dev/null || status=$?
          if [ -n "$timescaledb" ]; then
            echo "ALTER SYSTEM RESET timescaledb.restoring;" | sql postgres >/dev/null
            echo "SELECT pg_reload_conf();" | sql postgres >/dev/null
            for database in $(databases); do
              echo "SELECT timescaledb_post_restore() FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'timescaledb';" | sql "$database" >/dev/null
              echo "ALTER DATABASE \"$database\" RESET timescaledb.restoring;" | sql "$database" >/dev/null
            done
          fi
          exit "$status"
        - dokku-postgres-upgrade-import
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
        PGOPTIONS: "-c client_min_messages=warning"

    # what the data needs of the image a service is moved onto, read and
    # checked before anything of the service is touched. timescaledb only
    # restores a dump into the version of the extension that made it, so each
    # version a database runs is printed, and the check compares it with the
    # version the new image installs. Every postgres definition carries the
    # same text, which a test holds them to, and both do nothing where the
    # extension is not installed.
    requires:
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          set -e
          sql() {
            psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -qtAX -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d "$1"
          }
          versions=""
          for database in $(echo "SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datallowconn ORDER BY datname;" | sql postgres); do
            versions="$versions$(echo "SELECT 'timescaledb ' || extversion FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'timescaledb';" | sql "$database")
          "
          done
          printf '%s' "$versions" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u
        - dokku-postgres-upgrade-requires
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
    check:
      stdin: true
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          set -e
          while read -r name version; do
            [ -n "$name" ] || continue
            sharedir="$(pg_config --sharedir 2>/dev/null || true)"
            control="$sharedir/extension/$name.control"
            if [ -z "$sharedir" ] || [ ! -f "$control" ]; then
              echo "the data uses $name $version, which the new image does not install" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            installs="$(sed -n "s/^default_version *= *'\(.*\)'.*/\1/p" "$control")"
            if [ "$installs" != "$version" ]; then
              echo "the data uses $name $version, but the new image installs $name $installs, and a dump is only restored into the version that made it. Run ALTER EXTENSION $name UPDATE in each database on the current definition, or upgrade onto an image that installs $name $version" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
        - dokku-postgres-upgrade-check

  # the certificate the server was started with, so that a client off the host
  # can verify it is talking to this service. Read from the running container
  # rather than the host, which keeps it following a moved certs volume
  custom_commands:
    certificate:
      description: print the certificate the {{.Title}} service encrypts connections with
      documentation: |
        print the certificate the {{.Title}} service encrypts connections with
        > NOTE: the service must be running
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:certificate lollipop
        save it to verify the server from a client off the host
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:certificate lollipop > server.crt
      exec: ["cat", "{{ .Target.certs }}/server.crt"]

    # the data an upgrade kept aside belongs to the postgres user, so it is
    # removed from a container running as root rather than from the host. Only
    # the directories an upgrade names are matched, and each is printed as it
    # goes
    upgrade-cleanup:
      description: remove the data an upgrade across a major version kept aside
      documentation: |
        remove the data an upgrade across a major version kept aside
        > NOTE: the service must be running
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:upgrade-cleanup lollipop
      mode: sidecar
      user: "0"
      entrypoint: ""
      volumes:
        - type: bind
          source: "{{ .HostRoot }}"
          target: /service
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        - find /service -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'data.*' -print -exec rm -rf {} +

  # written the way a command's documentation is: every sentence ends in a
  # period, since prose lines run together, and inline code is quoted
  documentation:
    - title: Encrypting connections with TLS
      body: |
        every {{.Title}} service is created with a self-signed certificate, and the server encrypts any connection whose client asks it to.
        the certificate and its key are kept in '/var/lib/dokku/services/{{.CommandPrefix}}/lollipop/certs', and are kept when the service is rebuilt or upgraded.
        clients such as psql ask for an encrypted connection by default, but fall back to an unencrypted one when the server does not offer it.
        to refuse an unencrypted connection instead, add 'sslmode=require' to the dsn the service is exposed at:
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:info lollipop --exposed-dsn
            postgres://postgres:PASSWORD@db.example.com:5432/lollipop?sslmode=require
        to also check that the client is talking to this service, save its certificate and have the client verify the server with it.
        the certificate names no host, so 'sslmode=verify-ca' works where 'sslmode=verify-full' does not:
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:certificate lollipop > server.crt
            postgres://postgres:PASSWORD@db.example.com:5432/lollipop?sslmode=verify-ca&sslrootcert=server.crt
        to use a certificate of your own, write it and its key over the ones the service was created with as root, and restart the service.
        writing over the files rather than replacing them keeps the owner and mode the server needs to read its key:
            sudo sh -c 'cat server.crt > /var/lib/dokku/services/{{.CommandPrefix}}/lollipop/certs/server.crt'
            sudo sh -c 'cat server.key > /var/lib/dokku/services/{{.CommandPrefix}}/lollipop/certs/server.key'
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:restart lollipop

    # the image makes the database from the environment its first start sees,
    # so the only way to choose these is the custom env the service is made with
    - title: Choosing the database encoding and locale
      body: |
        the database is made the first time the service starts, with the encoding and locale of its container, which are utf8 and 'en_US.utf8' unless the custom environment says otherwise.
        a custom environment that only sets 'LC_ALL=C' leaves the database in the SQL_ASCII encoding, which stores bytes rather than utf8 text.
        to choose both, give the arguments 'initdb' takes in POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS when the service is created:
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:create lollipop --custom-env "POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS=--encoding=UTF8 --locale=C"
        they are only read when the data directory is first made, so changing the custom environment of an existing service leaves its database as it was.
        to move a database to another encoding or locale, create a service with the new ones and import an export of the old service into it:
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:export lollipop > lollipop.dump
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:create lollipop-utf8 --custom-env "POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS=--encoding=UTF8 --locale=C"
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:import lollipop-utf8 < lollipop.dump

    # what an upgrade across a major version does with the data, which is not
    # something the upgrade command's own documentation can say for every
    # datastore
    - title: Upgrading across a major version
      body: |
        an upgrade that moves a service to another major version, or onto another flavor, carries its data across rather than mounting it where the new version would not read it.
        the linked apps are stopped while the data is copied, so the upgrade has to be given '--restart-apps':
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:upgrade lollipop --definition postgres-18 --restart-apps
        onto a newer major of the official image the data is copied with 'pg_upgrade', which needs as much free disk as the data takes up.
        every other move exports every database and role from the old version with 'pg_dumpall' and replays it into the new one.
        a move that fails puts the service back on the version it ran, with the data it had.
        the old data is kept in a 'data.<definition>.<timestamp>' directory beside the service's data, and is removed once the upgrade is confirmed:
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:upgrade-cleanup lollipop

  commands:
    # the password goes in PGPASSWORD rather than on the command line, which is
    # what the bash plugin does too
    connect:
      exec: ["psql", "-v", "ON_ERROR_STOP=1", "-h", "localhost", "-U", "postgres", "{{ .Database }}"]
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
        LANG: C.UTF-8
        LC_ALL: C.UTF-8

    export:
      extra_args: true
      exec: ["pg_dump", "-Fc", "--no-acl", "--no-owner", "-h", "localhost", "-U", "postgres", "-w", "{{ .Database }}"]
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

      # every database but the templates, and the maintenance database unless
      # it is the service's own, as plain sql that psql loads. pg_dumpall is
      # not used because it dumps the roles too, and loading them would set the
      # postgres password to the one the dump was taken with, leaving every
      # linked app holding the wrong one. Each database is dropped and made
      # again from template0 with the encoding and locale it had, the way reset
      # makes it, and marked as restoring until it is loaded, which keeps the
      # timescaledb background workers from writing into its catalog while the
      # dump copies it back. The databases are owned by postgres, as the dump
      # carries no owners. The locale columns are read through the row as json,
      # since each major names them differently and fourteen has none of them:
      # a column one major lacks reads as null rather than failing the query.
      # Every postgres definition carries the same text, which a test holds
      # them to.
      all_databases:
        extra_args: true
        exec:
          - sh
          - -c
          - |
            set -e
            own="$1"
            shift
            sql() {
              psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -qtAX -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d template1 "$@"
            }
            databases="$(sql -v "own=$own" <<'SQL'
            SELECT datname FROM pg_database
             WHERE NOT datistemplate AND (datname <> 'postgres' OR datname = :'own')
             ORDER BY datname;
            SQL
            )"
            printf '%s\n' "$databases" | while IFS= read -r database; do
              sql -v "database=$database" <<'SQL'
            SELECT format('DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS %I WITH (FORCE);', datname) || chr(10)
                || format('CREATE DATABASE %I TEMPLATE template0 ENCODING %L LC_COLLATE %L LC_CTYPE %L',
                          datname, pg_encoding_to_char(encoding), datcollate, datctype)
                || CASE fields ->> 'datlocprovider'
                     WHEN 'i' THEN format(' LOCALE_PROVIDER icu ICU_LOCALE %L', coalesce(fields ->> 'datlocale', fields ->> 'daticulocale'))
                       || CASE WHEN fields ->> 'daticurules' IS NULL THEN '' ELSE format(' ICU_RULES %L', fields ->> 'daticurules') END
                     WHEN 'b' THEN format(' LOCALE_PROVIDER builtin BUILTIN_LOCALE %L', fields ->> 'datlocale')
                     WHEN 'c' THEN ' LOCALE_PROVIDER libc'
                     ELSE ''
                   END || ';' || chr(10)
                || format('ALTER DATABASE %I SET timescaledb.restoring = %L;', datname, 'on') || chr(10)
                || format('\connect %I', datname)
              FROM pg_database d, to_jsonb(d) AS fields WHERE datname = :'database';
            SQL
              pg_dump -Fp --no-acl --no-owner -h localhost -U postgres -w "$@" "$database"
              sql -v "database=$database" <<'SQL'
            SELECT format('ALTER DATABASE %I RESET timescaledb.restoring;', datname) || chr(10)
                || 'SELECT pg_catalog.format(''SELECT %I.timescaledb_post_restore();'', n.nspname)'
                || ' FROM pg_catalog.pg_extension e JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.oid = e.extnamespace'
                || ' WHERE e.extname = ''timescaledb'' \gexec'
              FROM pg_database WHERE datname = :'database';
            SQL
            done
          - dokku-postgres-export-all
          - "{{ .Database }}"
        env:
          PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

    import:
      extra_args: true
      stdin: true
      exec: ["pg_restore", "-h", "localhost", "-cO", "--if-exists", "-d", "{{ .Database }}", "-U", "postgres", "-w"]
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

      # a dump of every database, which drops and makes each database in it
      # again, so it is loaded from template1 rather than from any database it
      # might drop. A load that stops part way leaves a database it made marked
      # as restoring, where timescaledb runs no background workers, so the mark
      # is cleared whether the load worked or not. Every postgres definition
      # carries the same text, which a test holds them to.
      all_databases:
        extra_args: true
        stdin: true
        exec:
          - sh
          - -c
          - |
            status=0
            psql -X -q -o /dev/null -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -h localhost -U postgres -w -d template1 "$@" || status=$?
            psql -X -q -o /dev/null -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -h localhost -U postgres -w -d template1 <<'SQL' || exit $?
            SELECT format('ALTER DATABASE %I RESET timescaledb.restoring', d.datname)
              FROM pg_db_role_setting s JOIN pg_database d ON d.oid = s.setdatabase
             WHERE s.setrole = 0 AND 'timescaledb.restoring=on' = ANY (s.setconfig) \gexec
            SQL
            exit "$status"
          - dokku-postgres-import-all
        env:
          PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

    # the database is dropped and made again from template0 with the owner,
    # encoding and locale it had, rather than emptied, so nothing an app made in
    # it survives. WITH (FORCE) ends the sessions linked apps hold open, which
    # would otherwise refuse the drop. The extensions it had are made again at
    # the image's default version, timescaledb first and in a session of its
    # own, since the rest may build on it and it expects to be the first thing a
    # session loads. Settings made with ALTER DATABASE and grants on the database
    # itself are not carried over.
    #
    # the create statement is read before anything is dropped, so a database
    # that cannot be described is left alone. The locale columns are read
    # through the row as json, the way the export of every database reads them,
    # since each major names them differently. A service named postgres has the
    # maintenance database as its own, so the drop is run from template1 instead.
    # Written inline rather than shipped as a script, since a script is only
    # mounted into a container made after it was added, and a reset runs in the
    # container the service already has. Every postgres definition carries the
    # same text, which a test holds them to.
    reset:
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          set -e
          database="$1"
          maintenance=postgres
          if [ "$database" = postgres ]; then
            maintenance=template1
          fi
          sql() {
            psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -qtAX -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -v "database=$database" -d "$1"
          }
          timescaledb="$(sql "$database" <<'SQL'
          SELECT 1 FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'timescaledb';
          SQL
          )"
          extensions="$(sql "$database" <<'SQL'
          SELECT format('CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS %I CASCADE;', extname)
            FROM pg_extension WHERE extname NOT IN ('plpgsql', 'timescaledb') ORDER BY oid;
          SQL
          )"
          sql "$maintenance" >/dev/null <<'SQL'
          SELECT format('CREATE DATABASE %I OWNER %I TEMPLATE template0 ENCODING %L LC_COLLATE %L LC_CTYPE %L',
                   datname, pg_get_userbyid(datdba), pg_encoding_to_char(encoding), datcollate, datctype)
                 || CASE fields ->> 'datlocprovider'
                      WHEN 'i' THEN format(' LOCALE_PROVIDER icu ICU_LOCALE %L', coalesce(fields ->> 'datlocale', fields ->> 'daticulocale'))
                        || CASE WHEN fields ->> 'daticurules' IS NULL THEN '' ELSE format(' ICU_RULES %L', fields ->> 'daticurules') END
                      WHEN 'b' THEN format(' LOCALE_PROVIDER builtin BUILTIN_LOCALE %L', fields ->> 'datlocale')
                      WHEN 'c' THEN ' LOCALE_PROVIDER libc'
                      ELSE ''
                    END AS create_database
            FROM pg_database d, to_jsonb(d) AS fields WHERE datname = :'database' \gset
          DROP DATABASE :"database" WITH (FORCE);
          SELECT :'create_database' \gexec
          SQL
          if [ -n "$timescaledb" ]; then
            echo "CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb CASCADE;" | sql "$database" >/dev/null
          fi
          if [ -n "$extensions" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$extensions" | sql "$database" >/dev/null
          fi
        - dokku-postgres-reset
        - "{{ .Database }}"
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
        PGOPTIONS: "-c client_min_messages=warning"

  # the templates every new database is copied from. postgres is left out: it
  # is only the default database, and a service named after it works
  reserved_names: [template0, template1]

---
services:
  postgres:
    image: "{{ .Image }}:{{ .ImageVersion }}"

    # the image creates the database and the account from these during its own
    # initialisation, which is why there is no step afterwards to make them
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: "{{ .Database }}"
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

    # ssl is turned on by the server's own options rather than by editing the
    # configuration file it writes during initialisation. The bash plugin has
    # to pause the service, patch that file and start it again, because the
    # file does not exist until the service has run once.
    command:
      - postgres
      - -c
      - ssl=on
      - -c
      - "ssl_cert_file={{ .Target.certs }}/server.crt"
      - -c
      - "ssl_key_file={{ .Target.certs }}/server.key"
      - -c
      - ssl_ciphers=AES256+EECDH:AES256+EDH

    volumes:
      # where postgres kept its data before eighteen, which is the whole
      # reason this line has a definition of its own
      - type: bind
        source: "{{ .HostRoot }}/data"
        target: /var/lib/postgresql/data
      - type: bind
        source: "{{ .HostRoot }}/certs"
        target: /certs

    ports:
      - name: native
        target: 5432
        primary: true

x-dokku:
  plugin: postgres
  title: Postgres
  scheme: postgres

  # DATABASE rather than POSTGRES: a linked app gets DATABASE_URL, which is
  # what postgres, mysql and mariadb all hand over
  alias: DATABASE
  alt_alias: DOKKU_POSTGRES

  # the account is the image's own superuser rather than one named for the
  # service, which is what the bash plugin hands over
  dsn: "{{ .Scheme }}://postgres:{{ .Secret.password }}@{{ .Host }}:{{ .Port.native }}/{{ .Database }}"

  wait: native

  secrets:
    password:
      file: PASSWORD
      length: 16
      env: SERVICE_PASSWORD

      # the image only reads POSTGRES_PASSWORD when it makes the cluster, so a
      # new password is given to the role by the server itself. The statement
      # is written to psql's stdin rather than passed as an argument, so the
      # password stays out of the container's process table. Every postgres
      # definition carries the same text, which a test holds them to.
      change:
        exec:
          - sh
          - -c
          - |
            set -e
            password="$(printf '%s' "$NEW_PASSWORD" | sed "s/'/''/g")"
            printf "ALTER ROLE postgres PASSWORD '%s';\n" "$password" |
              psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -qtAX -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d postgres >/dev/null
          - dokku-postgres-change-password
        env:
          PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
          NEW_PASSWORD: "{{ .NewSecret }}"

  hooks:
    pre_create:
      # the certificate, made before the service runs rather than after. It is
      # left alone once it exists, so a service keeps the identity it was
      # created with rather than being given a new one each time its container
      # is remade.
      user: "0"
      entrypoint: ""
      volumes:
        - type: bind
          source: "{{ .HostRoot }}/certs"
          target: /certs
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        # postgres refuses to start on a key anyone but its own user can read
        # the two files change hands, but the directory holding them stays
        # with dokku: postgres only ever stats the key, and a directory owned
        # by the server would leave destroy unable to unlink what is inside it
        - >-
          test -f /certs/server.key ||
          (openssl req -new -newkey rsa:4096 -x509 -days 365000 -nodes
          -out /certs/server.crt -keyout /certs/server.key -batch >/dev/null 2>&1);
          chown 999:999 /certs/server.key /certs/server.crt &&
          chmod 600 /certs/server.key && chmod 644 /certs/server.crt

  # a service moved onto this definition from another postgres definition has
  # its data carried across: a major version cannot read another's cluster, and
  # a flavor's extensions are only in its own image. The old data directory is
  # kept aside under the service root until upgrade-cleanup removes it.
  upgrade:
    migrate: true

    # every database and role the cluster holds, rather than the one database
    # the export subcommand dumps, so that nothing an app or an operator made
    # beside it is left behind in the data kept aside. --clean drops what the
    # new cluster made of its own before it is made again from the dump.
    export:
      exec: ["pg_dumpall", "-h", "localhost", "-U", "postgres", "-w", "--clean", "--if-exists"]
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

    # the dump is replayed from the maintenance database, which pg_dumpall
    # drops and makes again from whichever database it last connected to. The
    # superuser it is replayed as already exists and cannot be dropped, so the
    # two statements that would try are left out of the roles at the top of the
    # dump, before its first \connect and so before any of its rows.
    #
    # an image may make template databases of its own when the cluster is
    # first made, as postgis does with template_postgis, and a template cannot
    # be dropped. pg_dumpall only clears template1's flag before dropping it, so
    # every other template the new cluster has is made an ordinary database
    # first. The dump makes each template the old cluster had a template again,
    # and one only the new image made stays an ordinary database.
    #
    # timescaledb's catalog has to be restored with its workers stopped and
    # its triggers off, which timescaledb_pre_restore does for a database. The
    # dump drops and makes every database again, so restoring is also turned on
    # for the whole server until the dump is in, and each database is told the
    # restore is over afterwards. Every postgres definition carries the same
    # text, which a test holds them to, and the timescaledb steps do nothing on
    # an image without the extension.
    import:
      stdin: true
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          set -e
          sql() {
            psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -qtAX -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d "$1"
          }
          databases() {
            echo "SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datallowconn ORDER BY datname;" | sql postgres
          }
          timescaledb="$(echo "SELECT 1 FROM pg_available_extensions WHERE name = 'timescaledb';" | sql postgres)"
          if [ -n "$timescaledb" ]; then
            echo "ALTER SYSTEM SET timescaledb.restoring = on;" | sql postgres >/dev/null
            echo "SELECT pg_reload_conf();" | sql postgres >/dev/null
            for database in $(databases); do
              echo "SELECT timescaledb_pre_restore() FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'timescaledb';" | sql "$database" >/dev/null
            done
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "SELECT format('ALTER DATABASE %I IS_TEMPLATE false', datname) FROM pg_database WHERE datistemplate AND datname NOT IN ('template0', 'template1') \gexec" | sql postgres >/dev/null
          status=0
          awk -v user=postgres '
            /^\\connect / { connected = 1 }
            !connected && ($0 == "CREATE ROLE " user ";" || $0 == "DROP ROLE IF EXISTS " user ";") { next }
            { print }
          ' | psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d postgres >/dev/null || status=$?
          if [ -n "$timescaledb" ]; then
            echo "ALTER SYSTEM RESET timescaledb.restoring;" | sql postgres >/dev/null
            echo "SELECT pg_reload_conf();" | sql postgres >/dev/null
            for database in $(databases); do
              echo "SELECT timescaledb_post_restore() FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'timescaledb';" | sql "$database" >/dev/null
              echo "ALTER DATABASE \"$database\" RESET timescaledb.restoring;" | sql "$database" >/dev/null
            done
          fi
          exit "$status"
        - dokku-postgres-upgrade-import
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
        PGOPTIONS: "-c client_min_messages=warning"

    # what the data needs of the image a service is moved onto, read and
    # checked before anything of the service is touched. timescaledb only
    # restores a dump into the version of the extension that made it, so each
    # version a database runs is printed, and the check compares it with the
    # version the new image installs. Every postgres definition carries the
    # same text, which a test holds them to, and both do nothing where the
    # extension is not installed.
    requires:
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          set -e
          sql() {
            psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -qtAX -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d "$1"
          }
          versions=""
          for database in $(echo "SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datallowconn ORDER BY datname;" | sql postgres); do
            versions="$versions$(echo "SELECT 'timescaledb ' || extversion FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'timescaledb';" | sql "$database")
          "
          done
          printf '%s' "$versions" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u
        - dokku-postgres-upgrade-requires
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
    check:
      stdin: true
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          set -e
          while read -r name version; do
            [ -n "$name" ] || continue
            sharedir="$(pg_config --sharedir 2>/dev/null || true)"
            control="$sharedir/extension/$name.control"
            if [ -z "$sharedir" ] || [ ! -f "$control" ]; then
              echo "the data uses $name $version, which the new image does not install" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            installs="$(sed -n "s/^default_version *= *'\(.*\)'.*/\1/p" "$control")"
            if [ "$installs" != "$version" ]; then
              echo "the data uses $name $version, but the new image installs $name $installs, and a dump is only restored into the version that made it. Run ALTER EXTENSION $name UPDATE in each database on the current definition, or upgrade onto an image that installs $name $version" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
        - dokku-postgres-upgrade-check

    # pg_upgrade from the image tianon publishes for each pair of majors, which
    # carries both servers' binaries as $PGBINOLD and $PGBINNEW. It only exists
    # for the official image, so the flavors export and import instead. Copy
    # mode rather than --link, so that the data kept aside still starts if
    # anything after this fails. Only the pairs onto eighteen are published for
    # arm64, so on an arm64 host a step onto an older major fails and the data
    # is exported and imported instead.
    #
    # the new cluster is made to match the old one's checksums, which
    # pg_upgrade refuses to mismatch. Eighteen turns them on by default and is
    # the first whose initdb can be told to leave them off, so that is only
    # asked of an initdb that knows it. The new cluster is also given the old
    # one's pg_hba.conf, since a plain initdb only trusts local connections and
    # the apps linked to the service would be refused. Every step carries the
    # same script, which a test holds them to.
    from:
      postgres-14:
        image: tianon/postgres-upgrade:14-to-16
        user: "0"
        volumes:
          - type: bind
            source: "{{ .HostRoot }}"
            target: /service
        env:
          PGDATAOLD: "/service/{{ .PreviousData }}"
          PGDATANEW: /service/data
        exec:
          - bash
          - -c
          - |
            set -e
            if ! "$PGBINOLD/pg_controldata" "$PGDATAOLD" | grep -q '^Data page checksum version: *0$'; then
              export POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS=--data-checksums
            elif "$PGBINNEW/initdb" --help | grep -q -- --no-data-checksums; then
              export POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS=--no-data-checksums
            fi
            docker-upgrade pg_upgrade
            cp "$PGDATAOLD/pg_hba.conf" "$PGDATANEW/pg_hba.conf"
            chown postgres:postgres "$PGDATANEW/pg_hba.conf"
      postgres-15:
        image: tianon/postgres-upgrade:15-to-16
        user: "0"
        volumes:
          - type: bind
            source: "{{ .HostRoot }}"
            target: /service
        env:
          PGDATAOLD: "/service/{{ .PreviousData }}"
          PGDATANEW: /service/data
        exec:
          - bash
          - -c
          - |
            set -e
            if ! "$PGBINOLD/pg_controldata" "$PGDATAOLD" | grep -q '^Data page checksum version: *0$'; then
              export POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS=--data-checksums
            elif "$PGBINNEW/initdb" --help | grep -q -- --no-data-checksums; then
              export POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS=--no-data-checksums
            fi
            docker-upgrade pg_upgrade
            cp "$PGDATAOLD/pg_hba.conf" "$PGDATANEW/pg_hba.conf"
            chown postgres:postgres "$PGDATANEW/pg_hba.conf"

  # the certificate the server was started with, so that a client off the host
  # can verify it is talking to this service. Read from the running container
  # rather than the host, which keeps it following a moved certs volume
  custom_commands:
    certificate:
      description: print the certificate the {{.Title}} service encrypts connections with
      documentation: |
        print the certificate the {{.Title}} service encrypts connections with
        > NOTE: the service must be running
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:certificate lollipop
        save it to verify the server from a client off the host
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:certificate lollipop > server.crt
      exec: ["cat", "{{ .Target.certs }}/server.crt"]

    # the data an upgrade kept aside belongs to the postgres user, so it is
    # removed from a container running as root rather than from the host. Only
    # the directories an upgrade names are matched, and each is printed as it
    # goes
    upgrade-cleanup:
      description: remove the data an upgrade across a major version kept aside
      documentation: |
        remove the data an upgrade across a major version kept aside
        > NOTE: the service must be running
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:upgrade-cleanup lollipop
      mode: sidecar
      user: "0"
      entrypoint: ""
      volumes:
        - type: bind
          source: "{{ .HostRoot }}"
          target: /service
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        - find /service -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'data.*' -print -exec rm -rf {} +

  # written the way a command's documentation is: every sentence ends in a
  # period, since prose lines run together, and inline code is quoted
  documentation:
    - title: Encrypting connections with TLS
      body: |
        every {{.Title}} service is created with a self-signed certificate, and the server encrypts any connection whose client asks it to.
        the certificate and its key are kept in '/var/lib/dokku/services/{{.CommandPrefix}}/lollipop/certs', and are kept when the service is rebuilt or upgraded.
        clients such as psql ask for an encrypted connection by default, but fall back to an unencrypted one when the server does not offer it.
        to refuse an unencrypted connection instead, add 'sslmode=require' to the dsn the service is exposed at:
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:info lollipop --exposed-dsn
            postgres://postgres:PASSWORD@db.example.com:5432/lollipop?sslmode=require
        to also check that the client is talking to this service, save its certificate and have the client verify the server with it.
        the certificate names no host, so 'sslmode=verify-ca' works where 'sslmode=verify-full' does not:
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:certificate lollipop > server.crt
            postgres://postgres:PASSWORD@db.example.com:5432/lollipop?sslmode=verify-ca&sslrootcert=server.crt
        to use a certificate of your own, write it and its key over the ones the service was created with as root, and restart the service.
        writing over the files rather than replacing them keeps the owner and mode the server needs to read its key:
            sudo sh -c 'cat server.crt > /var/lib/dokku/services/{{.CommandPrefix}}/lollipop/certs/server.crt'
            sudo sh -c 'cat server.key > /var/lib/dokku/services/{{.CommandPrefix}}/lollipop/certs/server.key'
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:restart lollipop

    # the image makes the database from the environment its first start sees,
    # so the only way to choose these is the custom env the service is made with
    - title: Choosing the database encoding and locale
      body: |
        the database is made the first time the service starts, with the encoding and locale of its container, which are utf8 and 'en_US.utf8' unless the custom environment says otherwise.
        a custom environment that only sets 'LC_ALL=C' leaves the database in the SQL_ASCII encoding, which stores bytes rather than utf8 text.
        to choose both, give the arguments 'initdb' takes in POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS when the service is created:
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:create lollipop --custom-env "POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS=--encoding=UTF8 --locale=C"
        they are only read when the data directory is first made, so changing the custom environment of an existing service leaves its database as it was.
        to move a database to another encoding or locale, create a service with the new ones and import an export of the old service into it:
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:export lollipop > lollipop.dump
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:create lollipop-utf8 --custom-env "POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS=--encoding=UTF8 --locale=C"
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:import lollipop-utf8 < lollipop.dump

    # what an upgrade across a major version does with the data, which is not
    # something the upgrade command's own documentation can say for every
    # datastore
    - title: Upgrading across a major version
      body: |
        an upgrade that moves a service to another major version, or onto another flavor, carries its data across rather than mounting it where the new version would not read it.
        the linked apps are stopped while the data is copied, so the upgrade has to be given '--restart-apps':
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:upgrade lollipop --definition postgres-18 --restart-apps
        onto a newer major of the official image the data is copied with 'pg_upgrade', which needs as much free disk as the data takes up.
        every other move exports every database and role from the old version with 'pg_dumpall' and replays it into the new one.
        a move that fails puts the service back on the version it ran, with the data it had.
        the old data is kept in a 'data.<definition>.<timestamp>' directory beside the service's data, and is removed once the upgrade is confirmed:
        dokku {{.CommandPrefix}}:upgrade-cleanup lollipop

  commands:
    # the password goes in PGPASSWORD rather than on the command line, which is
    # what the bash plugin does too
    connect:
      exec: ["psql", "-v", "ON_ERROR_STOP=1", "-h", "localhost", "-U", "postgres", "{{ .Database }}"]
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
        LANG: C.UTF-8
        LC_ALL: C.UTF-8

    export:
      extra_args: true
      exec: ["pg_dump", "-Fc", "--no-acl", "--no-owner", "-h", "localhost", "-U", "postgres", "-w", "{{ .Database }}"]
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

      # every database but the templates, and the maintenance database unless
      # it is the service's own, as plain sql that psql loads. pg_dumpall is
      # not used because it dumps the roles too, and loading them would set the
      # postgres password to the one the dump was taken with, leaving every
      # linked app holding the wrong one. Each database is dropped and made
      # again from template0 with the encoding and locale it had, the way reset
      # makes it, and marked as restoring until it is loaded, which keeps the
      # timescaledb background workers from writing into its catalog while the
      # dump copies it back. The databases are owned by postgres, as the dump
      # carries no owners. The locale columns are read through the row as json,
      # since each major names them differently and fourteen has none of them:
      # a column one major lacks reads as null rather than failing the query.
      # Every postgres definition carries the same text, which a test holds
      # them to.
      all_databases:
        extra_args: true
        exec:
          - sh
          - -c
          - |
            set -e
            own="$1"
            shift
            sql() {
              psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -qtAX -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d template1 "$@"
            }
            databases="$(sql -v "own=$own" <<'SQL'
            SELECT datname FROM pg_database
             WHERE NOT datistemplate AND (datname <> 'postgres' OR datname = :'own')
             ORDER BY datname;
            SQL
            )"
            printf '%s\n' "$databases" | while IFS= read -r database; do
              sql -v "database=$database" <<'SQL'
            SELECT format('DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS %I WITH (FORCE);', datname) || chr(10)
                || format('CREATE DATABASE %I TEMPLATE template0 ENCODING %L LC_COLLATE %L LC_CTYPE %L',
                          datname, pg_encoding_to_char(encoding), datcollate, datctype)
                || CASE fields ->> 'datlocprovider'
                     WHEN 'i' THEN format(' LOCALE_PROVIDER icu ICU_LOCALE %L', coalesce(fields ->> 'datlocale', fields ->> 'daticulocale'))
                       || CASE WHEN fields ->> 'daticurules' IS NULL THEN '' ELSE format(' ICU_RULES %L', fields ->> 'daticurules') END
                     WHEN 'b' THEN format(' LOCALE_PROVIDER builtin BUILTIN_LOCALE %L', fields ->> 'datlocale')
                     WHEN 'c' THEN ' LOCALE_PROVIDER libc'
                     ELSE ''
                   END || ';' || chr(10)
                || format('ALTER DATABASE %I SET timescaledb.restoring = %L;', datname, 'on') || chr(10)
                || format('\connect %I', datname)
              FROM pg_database d, to_jsonb(d) AS fields WHERE datname = :'database';
            SQL
              pg_dump -Fp --no-acl --no-owner -h localhost -U postgres -w "$@" "$database"
              sql -v "database=$database" <<'SQL'
            SELECT format('ALTER DATABASE %I RESET timescaledb.restoring;', datname) || chr(10)
                || 'SELECT pg_catalog.format(''SELECT %I.timescaledb_post_restore();'', n.nspname)'
                || ' FROM pg_catalog.pg_extension e JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.oid = e.extnamespace'
                || ' WHERE e.extname = ''timescaledb'' \gexec'
              FROM pg_database WHERE datname = :'database';
            SQL
            done
          - dokku-postgres-export-all
          - "{{ .Database }}"
        env:
          PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

    import:
      extra_args: true
      stdin: true
      exec: ["pg_restore", "-h", "localhost", "-cO", "--if-exists", "-d", "{{ .Database }}", "-U", "postgres", "-w"]
      env:
        PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

      # a dump of every database, which drops and makes each database in it
      # again, so it is loaded from template1 rather than from any database it
      # might drop. A load that stops part way leaves a database it made marked
      # as restoring, where timescaledb runs no background workers, so the mark
      # is cleared whether the load worked or not. Every postgres definition
      # carries the same text, which a test holds them to.
      all_databases:
        extra_args: true
        stdin: true
        exec:
          - sh
          - -c
          - |
            status=0
            psql -X -q -o /dev/null -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -h localhost -U postgres -w -d template1 "$@" || status=$?
            psql -X -q -o /dev/null -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -h localhost -U postgres -w -d template1 <<'SQL' || exit $?
            SELECT format('ALTER DATABASE %I RESET timescaledb.restoring', d.datname)
              FROM pg_db_role_setting s JOIN pg_database d ON d.oid = s.setdatabase
             WHERE s.setrole = 0 AND 'timescaledb.restoring=on' = ANY (s.setconfig) \gexec
            SQL
            exit "$status"
          - dokku-postgres-import-all
        env:
          PGPASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"

    # the database is dropped and made again from template0 with the owner,
    # encoding and locale it had, rather than emptied, so nothing an app made in
    # it survives. WITH (FORCE) ends the sessions linked apps hold open, which
    # would otherwise refuse the drop. The extensions it had are made again at
    # the image's default version, timescaledb first and in a session of its
    # own, since the rest may build on it and it expects to be the first thing a
    # session loads. Settings made with ALTER DATABASE and grants on the database
    # itself are not carried over.
    #
    # the create statement is read before anything is dropped, so a database
    # that cannot be described is left alone. The locale columns are read
    # through the row as json, the way the export of every database reads them,
    # since each major names them differently. A service named postgres has the
    # maintenance database as its own, so the drop is run from template1 instead.
    # Written inline rather than shipped as a script, since a script is only
    # mounted into a container made after it was added, and a reset runs in the
    # container the service already has. Every postgres definition carries the
    # same text, which a test holds them to.
    reset:
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          set -e
          database="$1"
          maintenance=postgres
          if [ "$database" = postgres ]; then
            maintenance=template1
          fi
          sql() {
            psql -h localhost -U postgres -w -qtAX -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -v "database=$database" -d "$1"
          }
          timescaledb="$(sql "$database" <<'SQL'
          SELECT 1 FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'timescaledb';
          SQL
          )"
          extensions="$(sql "$database" <<'SQL'
          SELECT format('CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS %I CASCADE;', extname)
            FROM pg_extension WHERE extname NOT IN ('plpgsql', 'timescaledb') ORDER BY oid;
          SQL
          )"
          sql "$maintenance" >/dev/null <<'SQL'
